propositions: Code review lacks a dedicated concurrency correctness criterion; security and performance overlays address only attacker-framed TOCTOU and load-shaped patterns, leaving unlocked-twin and true-race classes unowned

The overlay applies a lockset-first (Eraser/RacerD) deterministic two-tier lexical trigger: a committed high-precision tier fires on explicit synchronization primitives (Lock, flock, RwLock), while a project-extensible noisy tier in .rebar/criteria_routing.json catches repo-specific patterns like git rm+commit and index.lock TOCTOU

The committed tier deliberately does not fire on the codebase's modal unlocked-twin class (raw index writes, getmtime-then-remove), accepting documented recall boundary in exchange for portability; project-tier token vocabulary (e.g. .lock, stage_and_commit) must be configured locally
A project can extend built-in overlay vocabulary and applies_to globs through .rebar/criteria_routing.json without code changes; rebar dogfoods this mechanism with its own concurrency vocabulary
The overlay ships advisory (block_threshold 0.95, blocking_enabled false) pending calibration; blocking-flip is out of scope
Accepted v1 blind spots: no-twin races (twice-read patterns) and CI-level CAS/backoff judgment are lexical/judgment ceiling confirmed by independent survey analysis
